content:
Alex: OpsBot just flagged sustained GPU saturation in shared-pool-eu-west-1, looks like one tenant is driving 75% of queued tokens.
OpsBot: [alert] gpu-utilization > 92% (10m avg) on pool shared-pool-eu-west-1. queued_requests: 1200, tail_latency_p95: 1.8s.
Maria: Ugh, saw spike around 08:12 UTC. Are these long generations or lots of short chat calls?
Kevin: Mostly long-context reranks + streaming. Their KV cache hit is low.
Jia: Current admission is simple leaky-bucket per-tenant + global concurrency cap. No soft-holdback when pool is near-sat.
Omar: Proposal: introduce granular credit pools per-tenant-per-shard and a wakeup token that only allows new sessions when headroom exists. Soft-holdback instead of hard throttle so we avoid full ejections.
Alex: Sketch?
Omar: 1) Each shard holds N credits; tenants are assigned weights. 2) When shard queue depth > Q_high, new sessions consume a 'wake' token instead of direct admission. Wake tokens come from shard headroom and are rate-limited. 3) If queue spikes, start reclaiming credits from noisy tenants gradually (soft holdback) rather than immediate preemption.
Maria: How do wake tokens differ from current rate limits?
Omar: Wake tokens are ephemeral, owned by shard, not tenant. They represent "start capacity" and are only given if KV cache & GPU kernels likely match. So we bias towards warmups that won't thrash KV cache.
Kevin: Implementation detail: need fast counters in Redis or local shard ringbuf? Redis adds network hops. Any perf sketch?
Jia: We can keep counters local to the serving process and periodically delta-sync to Redis. For safety, use Redis only for global accounting + recovery. Local counters give O(1) checks for admission.
SRE-Oncall: Rollback story? If soft-holdback misbehaves we should auto-disable after 5m or on error budget breach.
Alex: Metrics to add: per-tenant queued_tokens, wake_tokens_given, credit_reclaim_rate, preempt_fallbacks. Also a heatmap of generator length vs cache_hit_ratio.
Maria: Cost tradeoff? Keeping headroom reduces throughput utilization. Ballpark impact?
Omar: Sim sim suggests reserving 6% headroom to eliminate 90% of noisy-induced tail spikes. For our fleet that's roughly +$6k/month in cloud GPU equivalent. (back-of-envelope)
Kevin: Sounds reasonable. Also need fairness rule: soft reclamation should consider recent latency SLAs — don't penalize low-latency tenants. Could use score = tenant_weight * recent_empirical_cost.
Jia: Pseudocode for admission check:
```
if shard.queue_depth > Q_high:
  if tenant.local_credit > 0 and shard.headroom_tokens > 0:
    grant_wake_token()
    tenant.local_credit -= 1
  else:
    answer_with_429_or_enqueue_low_priority()
else:
  normal_admit()
```
Kevin: For enqueuing low-priority, prefer background batch windows (non-interactive) so we don't block front-door chat.
SRE-Oncall: Can we test in staging? Need a canary where noisy tenant is simulated. Also chaos test with KV cache miss flood.
Alex: Next steps: Omar & Jia build prototype (local counters + wake token logic) behind a feature flag, Kevin wires metrics + dashboards, Maria does canary plan & cost analysis, SRE-Oncall prepares rollback triggers.
Maria: One more: network egress/backpressure interactions — if shard is network-bound, wake tokens should consider net_bandwidth_util too.
Omar: Good call. Add net_bandwidth_util check to wake token eligibility.
Kevin: I'll add a small alert: if credit_reclaim_rate > X for 3m, send to #incidents as early warning.
Alex: Timeline? Can we have a lab demo in one week and a soft canary in two?
Jia: I'll aim for a prototype in 5d.
Omar: I'll document the algorithm in a short RFC and include metric names + dashboard mock.
SRE-Oncall: Marking this thread for follow-up next on-call shift. :white_check_mark:
Maria: Thanks everyone.
Alex: TL;DR: implement granular per-shard credits + wakeup tokens + soft reclamation to reduce noisy-neighbor tail latency, canary + rollback plan, metrics + alerting.
